title: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: A Statistical Perspective
abstract: arXiv:2604.02507v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has emerged as a central framework for aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences. Despite its practical success, RLHF raises fundamental statistical questions because it relies on noisy, subjective, and heterogeneous feedback to learn reward models and optimize policies. This survey provides a statistical perspective on RLHF, focusing primarily on LLM alignment. We introduce the main components of RLHF, including supervised fine-tuning, reward modeling, and policy optimization, and relate them to familiar statistical concepts such as the Bradley-Terry-Luce (BTL) model, latent utility estimation, active learning, experimental design, and uncertainty quantification. We review methods for learning reward functions from pairwise preference data and for optimizing policies through both two-stage RLHF pipelines and emerging one-stage approaches such as direct prefer

translated_title: 基于人类反馈的强化学习：统计视角
translated_abstract: 基于人类反馈的强化学习（RLHF）已成为将大语言模型（LLM）与人类偏好对齐的核心框架。尽管在实践中取得了成功，RLHF由于依赖嘈杂、主观且异构的反馈来学习奖励模型并优化策略，因而引发了一些根本性的统计学问题。本综述从统计学的视角审视RLHF，主要聚焦于大语言模型的对齐。我们介绍了RLHF的主要组成部分，包括监督微调、奖励建模和策略优化，并将它们与人们熟知的统计概念联系起来，如Bradley-Terry-Luce（BTL）模型、潜效用估计、主动学习、实验设计和不确定性量化。我们回顾了从成对偏好数据中学习奖励函数的方法，以及通过两阶段RLHF流程和新兴的一阶段方法（如直接偏好优化）来优化策略的相关方法。
tldr: 本综述首次系统地从统计学视角梳理了RLHF框架，将其核心组成部分（监督微调、奖励建模与策略优化）与BTL模型、潜效用估计、主动学习、实验设计和不确定性量化等经典统计概念联系起来。
en_tdlr: This survey provides a statistical perspective on RLHF, connecting its main components—supervised fine-tuning, reward modeling, and policy optimization—to established statistical concepts such as the Bradley-Terry-Luce model, latent utility estimation, active learning, and uncertainty quantification.
